_comment: DS4 machine tuning profiles. The first entry whose match{chip substring, min_ram_gib} fits this machine is applied: each env var is set as a DEFAULT (setenv overwrite=0), so anything you export yourself still wins. Generate/refresh an entry for your machine with ./tune_profile.sh. Order entries most-specific first.

_backends_reference._doc: Valid 'backend' values for prefill_by_tokens — the resident routed-MoE prefill algorithm, selected PER PREFILL CHUNK by token count. PRECEDENCE: (1) env param DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_BACKEND forces one backend for all chunks; (2) this prefill_by_tokens table (the loader encodes it into DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_PREFILL_BY_TOKENS and the engine resolves the backend by name per chunk); (3) the predefined env gates (NAX_HALF + MIN_TOKENS, to be phased out). Backends honored PER-CHUNK in the grouped path: mulmm, nax_half, nax_half_alu, nax_int8 (the table overrides the static env flags). NOT per-chunk-switchable here: ane_gpu is a separate dedup orchestrator, and ane_alu/ane_nax/pathc are unsupported in the grouped path — naming any of them in a range logs a one-time warning and falls back to the env gates. NAX backends are M5+ only (matmul2d); on M3/M4 they fall back to mul_mm_id. NAX-half additionally requires n_tokens % 64 == 0 (else the engine uses int8).

mulmm.desc: Upstream mul_mm_id grouped GPU matmul (pure ALU, no NAX). The 'ALU only' baseline. Works on all chips.

nax_int8.desc: NAX int8 matmul2d, compact-bridge fused-dequant. M5 LARGE-chunk winner.
nax_int8.env: DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_MPP_INT8_PREFILL=1 DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_MPP_COMPACT_BRIDGE=1 DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_MPP_FUSED_DEQUANT=1 (+MPP_FORCE=1 to ignore the auto min-tokens gate)

nax_half.desc: NAX half x half matmul2d (no fused gate+up).

nax_half_alu.desc: NAX-half + ALU, Plan A fused gate+up+swiglu. M5 SMALL-chunk winner. (FIXED 2026-06-01, commit aeea2b7: the fused kernel was reducing only 32 of K + dropping the routing weight -> divergent; now matches mulmm/nax_half exactly and is ~6% faster than plain nax_half at 4096. NOTE at HOT thermal nax_int8 can edge it out at small chunks; the <7680 vs int8 crossover is cool-tuned — re-bake if needed.)

pathc.desc: Path C: i8 in-kernel NAX-parallel-ALU full-fused.
pathc.note: ~tie with nax_int8 on M5 (no cross-kernel NAX/ALU overlap)

ane_gpu.desc: ANE hot experts + grouped GPU(ALU) cold. Correct. The dual-cluster ANE win is M3 Ultra; on M5 Max (single cluster) ANE is ~+6 t/s (GPU-encode-bound).

ane_alu.desc: ANE hot + grouped classic-int8 (mul_mm_id) cold. Correct — identical to ane_gpu's cold tail (the per-expert dedup compute it once used is broken and is no longer on this path).

ane_nax.desc: ANE hot + grouped NAX cold (resident NAX-half/int8 under the ANE skip mask). Correct (validate_ane_nax 8/8). NOT a throughput win yet on M5 Max: the cold tail runs SEQUENTIALLY after ANE drains, and resident-NAX cold is slower to encode than fused mul_mm_id, so ane_nax<ane_gpu (measured ctx16384: 207 vs 315 t/s). The win needs true ANE-parallel-NAX overlap (dispatch NAX before draining ANE) — not yet implemented. Off by default.
ane_nax.chips: M5+; correct but not faster (no overlap yet)

profiles._comment: M5 Max 128G, MEASURED (81G IQ2XXS, 45s cooldown, alone on box). CORRECTED 2026-06-01: (a) added DS4_METAL_PREFILL_CHUNK=16384 — without it a bare ./ds4 auto-caps the chunk to 4096 (<sync_max_tokens 7168) and the resident-NAX path takes the slow CPU<->GPU count-readback (map_wait) sync bridge; CTX_GROW_BLOCK is the KV-growth block, NOT the prefill chunk. (b) reverted the >1000->ane_gpu routing back to the NAX crossover: ane_gpu (ANE+GPU dedup) MEASURED 30-41% SLOWER on M5 single-cluster (ctx16384: ane_gpu 310 vs nax_half_alu 445 vs nax_int8 526 t/s) because ANE_HYBRID forces the 2048-token scratch tile -> sync bridge ON. prefill_by_tokens picks per prefill chunk: nax_half_alu below 7680 tok, nax_int8 at/above (crossover from 4096:316/269 .. 7168:423/366 half-wins .. 8192:378/500 int8-wins; loader maps to NAX_HALF_MAX_TOKENS=7680). With chunk 16384 production prefill resolves to nax_int8 (~526 hot). Verify with the 'resident-NAX tile n_tokens=.. sync-bridge=off' startup line. 2026-06-01 (2): <7680 was briefly switched to plain nax_half because the FUSED gate+up+swiglu kernel diverged. That kernel is now FIXED (commit aeea2b7 — it was reducing only 32 of K via a fixed K-tile + dropping the routing weight; rewritten to mirror the validated h_h_f matmul with dynamic_extent K + a weighted scatter). <7680 restored to nax_half_alu (matches mulmm exactly, ~6% faster than nax_half at 4096). HOT-thermal caveat: nax_int8 can beat nax_half_alu at small chunks when the box is hot; the cool-tuned crossover favors half_alu <7680 — re-bake with tune_profile.sh on a cool box to confirm.

M3 Ultra: NO NAX (matmul2d is M5-only via ds4_gpu_is_m5_device; nax_half_alu/nax_int8 silently fall back to mul_mm_id), so there is NO per-token GPU-backend split like the M5 entry — the routed GPU path is mul_mm_id at every chunk size, and a nax-style prefill_by_tokens would no-op. M3U's win is DUAL-CLUSTER ANE, gated PER-EXPERT by refs (no per-chunk-token ANE gate exists). refs ~= chunk_tokens/32, so prefill_by_tokens here is informational: it documents the token->refs mapping that ANE_MIN_REFS=64 implies (ANE auto-engages on chunks >~2048 tokens and scales up). To get MEASURED M3U numbers, run tune_profile.sh ON the M3U (this box is M5 Max; M3U cannot be benchmarked here). DS4_FLASH_MOE_ANE_DUAL=1 lights both ANE clusters on the SSD/slot-bank path. CORRECTED 2026-06-01: min_ram_gib 64->96 (M3 Ultra is 96G+; covers 128/256/512); added DS4_METAL_PREFILL_CHUNK=16384 + raised CTX_GROW_BLOCK to 16384 so the raw-KV window can hold a 16K chunk (else it clamps back to ~2048 — verify via the 'prefill chunk cap EFFECTIVE=' startup line). M3U does NOT use the resident-NAX sync bridge (mul_mm_id path), so 16K chunks help ANE engagement without the map_wait cost. UNVERIFIED on M3U hardware (this box is M5 Max) — RETEST on the M3 Ultra and re-bake with tune_profile.sh.

M5 Max 96G — mirrors the 128G entry (same single-ANE-cluster silicon; the ANE-slow finding is RAM-independent). CORRECTED 2026-06-01: was an ANE-dedup config (ane_gpu-style), which is 30-41% slower on M5 single-cluster; switched to the NAX resident config with DS4_METAL_PREFILL_CHUNK=16384 + nax_int8 routing for large chunks. 81G model fits in 96G. Retest/re-bake with tune_profile.sh on a 96G M5 Max if available.
